newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Pakistan newspapers - Sept 26.

text.p: Following are the leading stories in Pakistani newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- The Afghan Taleban militia said on Wednesday its forces had reached the eastern outskirts of Kabul and were battling government forces after capturing Pul-i-Charki village and the military academy. On Tuesday night it captured the government-held town of Sarobi.
- A Pakistani court ruled that a girl's marriage without the consent of her parents or legal guardians was void.
- The government is considering launching a massive clean-up operation against terrorists in the central province of Punjab.
- An independant study by the U.S.-based Soccer Industry Council of America has said that bonded child labour was not involved in football-making in Pakistan.
- Opposition leader Nawaz Sharif will call on President Farooq Leghari on Thursday to discuss political situation.
- Egypt has invited Pakistan to participate in the third Middle East economic summit in Cairo in November.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto will preside over an extraordinary meeting of the cabinet on Thursday.
- Opposition parties have given a call for a general strike on Thursday.
- The government has approved a $2.6 billion-1,609 km-42-inch oil pipeline from Turkmenistan to Pakistan.
- Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto will leave Pakistan on September 29 to visit Britain and the United States and to address the United Nations General Assembly on October 3.
- Pakistan's foreign exchange reserves stood at $1,230 million on Wednesday and there is no threat of default in debt repayment and no loan will be rescheduled.
- The state-run Oil and Gas Development Corporation is planning to disinvest 49 percent of its shares in the first quarter of 1997.
